attacks.claim: The Recent signers template renders the full name and postal code on a public page. This contradicts the agreed rule (first name, last initial and city at most) and the proposal's own description of the feature. It would expose EU and US signers' personal data as soon as the flag is on.

Publishing full names and postal codes of EU signers publicly breaches GDPR data minimisation and purpose limitation. It also violates the agreed public-list constraint. Petition signatures can also reveal political opinions, which are special-category data under GDPR.
attacks.evidence: Public "Recent signers" panel ... showing first name + last initial and city, so visitors can see momentum without exposing signers. (template shows s.full_name and s.postal_code)

attacks.claim: The newsletter opt-in is pre-ticked. GDPR requires consent to be a clear affirmative act, so this does not give valid consent. It is also bundled with marketing for 'others from' the organizer.

WCAG 2.1 AA was agreed for all public flows, but errors are shown only through a red border and background. The .form-error live region is never populated, and there is no aria-invalid or aria-describedby. Non-422 failures (409 duplicate, 500, network) produce no feedback at all. Required fields have no visible indicator, and novalidate removes native validation messages.
attacks.evidence:
for (const name of fields) form.elements[name].classList.add('is-invalid'); ...

... if (res.ok) window.location = ...

attacks.claim: The 409 duplicate case and other non-422 errors are unhandled, so the form silently does nothing. If a 422 returns an empty fields array, fields[0] is undefined and focus() throws. A network failure causes an unhandled rejection.
attacks.evidence: form.elements[fields[0]].focus(); ... Duplicate signature (same email) rejected with 409 | Pass

attacks.claim: Retention is defined only for unconfirmed signatures. There is no retention period, erasure or withdrawal path for confirmed signers' name, email and postal code, which GDPR requires. The 10s CDN cache also keeps a removed signer visible briefly.
attacks.evidence: Unconfirmed signatures are not counted and are purged after 7 days. ... Signer email and postal code are stored in `signatures`

attacks.claim: QA does not cover the privacy rule. The Recent signers panel is not tested, and the axe scan covers only the sign page. An automated scan does not establish WCAG 2.1 AA conformance, so the agreed accessibility requirement is unverified.
attacks.evidence: axe-core automated scan on sign page | 0 violations

attacks.claim: The panel uses s.city, but the form collects only a postal code. No city lookup or derivation is described, so the source of the value is undefined.
The load test measured signature writes only. Read traffic from 15s polling and the per-render recent_signers query is untested.
attacks.evidence: Load: 400 signatures/s sustained for 10 min, p95 210ms | Pass

attacks.claim: No alerting owner or on-call is named for the 24h watch. The rollback fallback ('Follow this petition') is not shown to have been tested.
attacks.evidence: Watch `sign_submit_error_rate` (< 0.5%) and confirmation email bounce rate (< 2%) for 24h.

attacks.claim: A flag flip stops new exposure but does not remediate personal data already published or cached during the 10% stage.
